checks.diagnosis: The prompt allows cuts that leave a clause or predicate syntactically incomplete by separating it from a required complement or reason clause, which yields high contradiction and kills the set.
checks.evidence: en_us_733, en_us_381, en_us_1199, en_us_1294, en_us_1636 — each shows the policy cutting so that the following words are required to complete the left clause (reason/complement/object), producing a high contra on that boundary.
checks.type_predicate: Positions immediately before a following phrase that is required to complete the preceding clause (a required complement or reason clause whose scope attaches to the left clause).

edit.text: Do not cut where the right-side begins a required complement/reason clause that completes the preceding predicate (i.e. leaves a clause or verb stranded awaiting 'that/because'/an object).

orders.diagnosis: When two candidate cuts are both allowed, the prompt prefers earlier splits that leave verbs or complements stranded instead of preserving verb+object; the prompt should prefer cuts that keep a verb with its required complement.
orders.evidence: en_us_633, en_us_381, en_us_1636 — in each sentence the label prefers the cut that preserves the verb together with its object/complement while the prompt preferred splitting the verb or leaving the complement isolated.
orders.type_predicate: Pairs of positions in the same clause where one cut separates a verb/auxiliary from its required object/complement and the other falls earlier (separating subject/adjunct from the verb).

edit.text: When one candidate splits a verb (or auxiliary) from its required object/complement and the other splits earlier adjunct/subject material, prefer the cut that keeps the verb with its complement.
